title: To amend the Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act to require the Secretary of Health and Human Services to consider certain recognized security practices of covered entities and business associates when making certain determinations, and for other purposes.
official_summary:
This bill addresses health information technology provisions concerning cybersecurity practices and information blocking.

The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) may reduce fines and penalties for violations of certain federal privacy standards for health information if an entity subject to those standards has adopted particular cybersecurity practices.

This bill also authorizes HHS's Office of the Inspector General to obtain information, assistance, and other support from federal agencies when investigating claims of information blocking by developers of, or entities offering, health information technologies.

Information blocking refers to a practice that is likely to interfere with, prevent, or materially discourage access, exchange, or use of electronic health information, such as the imposition of fees that make exchanging this information cost prohibitive.

summary.headline: A 2021 law requires HHS to consider good cybersecurity practices when deciding health data privacy penalties, and lets its inspector general get help investigating blocked health records.
summary.what_it_does: The law amends the HITECH Act, which covers electronic health records and privacy. When HHS decides on fines or penalties for violating federal health privacy rules, it must consider whether the organization had recognized security practices in place, and it may reduce penalties if it did. The law also lets HHS's Office of the Inspector General request information and support from other federal agencies when investigating information blocking, which is when health technology companies or providers unreasonably prevent people from accessing or sharing electronic health information, such as by charging fees that make exchange too costly.

who_it_affects.group: Hospitals, doctors' offices, and health plans covered by HIPAA
who_it_affects.how: If they are investigated or penalized for a privacy violation, HHS must consider whether they followed recognized cybersecurity practices, which can lead to lower fines.

who_it_affects.group: Business associates such as billing companies and cloud vendors that handle health data for providers
who_it_affects.how: They can also have their adopted recognized security practices weighed by HHS when penalties are set.

who_it_affects.group: Health IT developers and entities that offer health information technology
who_it_affects.how: They may face increased federal investigation support for claims that they block or discourage access to electronic health information.

who_it_affects.group: Patients and people whose health records are exchanged electronically
who_it_affects.how: The law aims to reduce information blocking that could limit their access to and sharing of their own electronic health information.
